clue.text: Displays a garment to provide a theatrical sensation

parts.note: displays (verb) means shows
a topper is a top hat, or a short loose coat worn over other clothes

explanation.surface: A performer flaunts an outfit to wow the theatre audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn so brilliant that the applause halts the performance is a theatrical sensation.

clue.text: Instrument which has a note without a beginning

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for the note is dropped, as it lacks its beginning

parts.note: sharp is a note raised by a semitone

explanation.surface: A musical instrument that lacks the start of a note.
explanation.definitionFit: A harp is a stringed musical instrument plucked with the fingers.

clue.text: Welfare which is the result of a blow

explanation.surface: Wellbeing that leaves a bruise.
explanation.definitionFit: Weal is an old word for wellbeing, as in the common weal; it is also a raised mark on the skin left by a whip or blow.

clue.text: Added up to a sober journalist

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes someone who never drinks
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Someone calculating a total for a reporter who stays off the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up a column is to sum it, so totted is a synonym for summed.

clue.text: Student of fossils gives a friend an eternity and the main point of an imperfect tool

parts.note: pal is an informal word for a friend
an aeon is an immensely long age

indicators.note: something imperfect is flawed or out of shape, so the letters of tool are rearranged

parts.note: the gist is the essential point of something

explanation.surface: A fossil expert is credited with friendship, endless time and the purpose of a broken implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imperfect' signals that the tool is broken, its letters rearranged as TOLO; the friend, eternity and point are ordinary synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: A palaeontologist is a scientist who studies prehistoric life through fossil remains.

clue.text: In Italian villa give thanks for a car

indicators.note: the word for thanks is placed in the name of the villa

parts.note: the Villa d'Este at Tivoli is a famous Italian villa
ta is an informal British way of saying thanks

explanation.surface: Someone at an Italian country house expresses gratitude for a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: An ESTATE car is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a type of car with a long body and rear door, a station wagon.

clue.text: Waylays flowers

explanation.surface: Ambushes blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttonhole someone is to detain them in conversation, waylay them; buttonholes are also flowers worn in a lapel.

clue.text: Organise it to rise in a variety of messy seat

indicators.note: the turned word is placed inside the shuffled letters
a variety offers the letters in a different arrangement, so these words are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading the word upwards, so it is turned round

explanation.surface: Tidy up by getting a chair out of an untidy pile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messy' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'a variety of' shuffles MESSY SEAT into SYSTEMASE, and 'to rise' gives TI, put 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To systematise is to arrange something according to a method, which is to order it.

clue.text: Town put underground

explanation.surface: A place laid in the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Bury is a town in Greater Manchester; to bury is also to inter or place beneath the soil.

clue.text: Protection provided in spear battle

indicators.note: the protection is supplied by these words once their letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Armour issued to a soldier fighting with spears.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no strong anagram signal: 'provided in' and the fighting sense of 'battle' suggest the letters of SPEAR BATTLE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A breastplate is a piece of armour that shields the chest.

clue.text: Let it stand among the waste to be removed

indicators.note: among signals that the answer lies within the run of letters across the words waste and to

explanation.surface: A plea to leave one item standing while the rubbish is cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the waste to be removed' paints a skip, but 'among' tells you to look inside 'waste to'; 'be removed' is padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is Latin for let it stand, the proofreading mark that restores a crossed-out passage.

clue.text: The doctrine of man's fear is what Franco might have used

parts.note: his means belonging to a man
panic is sudden overwhelming fear
an ism is any doctrine or creed

explanation.surface: A philosophy of masculine dread is credited to the Spanish dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: General Franco ruled Spain, so a Spanish turn of phrase is something he might have used.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hispanicism is a word or idiom borrowed from Spanish, the language of the dictator.

clue.text: Dimensions of the golfer's helpings

parts.note: a pro is a professional golfer attached to a club
portions are servings of food

explanation.surface: How big are the meals served to the man at the golf club?
explanation.definitionFit: Proportions means size or extent, as in a building of huge proportions.

clue.text: Returns when a tennis champion is in the middle

annotationWithheld.why: Returns when a tennis champion is in the middle (7): EVERT (Chris Evert) sits inside R...S, but no clue word other than the definition 'Returns' supplies R and S, so a word would do two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Returns when a tennis champion is in the middle

clue.text: Dish with batter and the opposite of victory

parts.note: a ram is a beast or engine that batters

indicators.note: the opposite direction, so the goddess's name is read from right to left

parts.note: Nike is the Greek goddess of victory

explanation.surface: A bowl of batter alongside defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the opposite of' turns NIKE into EKIN; 'batter' is the battering ram, not pancake mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramekin is a small ovenproof bowl used for baking and serving single portions.

clue.text: Shaped like a ball and starting to perish in confusion

annotationWithheld.why: Shaped like a ball and starting to perish in confusion (7): P (starting to perish) plus an anagram needs fodder such as RICHES, and no word of the clue as held supplies it; the clue looks cut short
annotationWithheld.clue: Shaped like a ball and starting to perish in confusion

clue.text: Favourite thoroughfare leads to encroachment

parts.note: in means popular or in favour, as with the in crowd
a road is a public thoroughfare

explanation.surface: A preferred route ends up trespassing.
explanation.definitionFit: An inroad is an advance into someone else's territory, an intrusion.

clue.text: A funny poem about a place in America. It has things named after it

definitions.text: It has things named after it

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the place
something funny is odd, so the letters of poem are rearranged

parts.note: NY is New York

explanation.surface: A comic verse about New York gives its name to things.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the second sentence; 'funny' gives EPOM and 'about' wraps it round New York's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponym is a person or place from whose name something else is derived.

clue.text: Spotted where letters are sent but narrowly defeated at the last

parts.note: pipped can mean marked with pips, spots like those on dice
letters are sent through the post

explanation.surface: Someone spotted at the mail office loses by a whisker.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beaten at the finishing line by a tiny margin is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: European who gives backing to a detective fellow

indicators.note: these words are written backwards, given a reversal

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British plain-clothes detectives
Ron is a man's name, used for any fellow

explanation.surface: A European supports a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator turns both pieces: CID + RON read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nordic person comes from Scandinavia or Finland, part of northern Europe.

clue.text: The insect is a low fellow in intelligence

indicators.note: the scoundrel is placed inside the agency

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A bug is a bounder working for the spies.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicada is a large insect known for its loud shrill chirping.

clue.text: Fierce ones see little gravity in rows

indicators.note: the symbol is placed inside the word for rows

parts.note: tiers are rows placed one above another
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: Wild animals find hardly any seriousness among the lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigers are big cats renowned for their ferocity, so fierce creatures.

clue.text: Town makes it up about one part of book

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: vol. is short for volume, one part of a book
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A town invents something about a section of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Tivoli is a town near Rome famous for its villas and gardens.

clue.text: Concerning an Egyptian flower

parts.note: a flower is read as something that flows, a river, so this means relating to the great river of Egypt

explanation.surface: Something about a bloom from Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Nilotic means of or relating to the River Nile and its region.

clue.text: Money keeps the company fashionable

parts.note: Co. is short for company
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Cash keeps the firm trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: Coin is metal currency, so cash.

clue.text: Make love but there is specific gravity about the negative

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes around the negative word

parts.note: SG is the standard abbreviation for specific gravity
no is the negative reply

explanation.surface: Romance is spoiled by physics and a refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make love' is used in its older sense of kiss and cuddle; to SNOG is British slang for that.
explanation.definitionFit: Snogging is kissing and cuddling, the old sense of courting.

clue.text: Something round for the dance

explanation.surface: A sphere for the formal party.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is a round object, and also a grand formal dance.

clue.text: American changed into acorn finial

indicators.note: changed tells us these letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A US citizen turns into a decorative acorn on a rooftop.
explanation.walkthrough: A finial is an ornament topping a roof or post, often acorn-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: A Californian is a native of California, a US state.

clue.text: Words set to music for a dynasty

explanation.surface: Lyrics for an imperial house.
explanation.definitionFit: A song is a lyric set to a tune; the Song dynasty ruled China from 960 to 1279.

clue.text: Very cheap beer but it helps to fill one out

definitions.text: it helps to fill one out

parts.note: a farthing was a quarter of an old British penny, the smallest coin, so a byword for cheapness
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Bargain-basement beer that makes you put on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: A FARTHINGALE was a hooped frame worn under Tudor skirts to make them stand out.
explanation.definitionFit: The hooped petticoat spread a woman's skirt wide, filling her figure out.
